arxiv-1512-01237.title: Quantum mechanics of 4-derivative theories
arxiv-1512-01237.creator: Alberto Salvio
arxiv-1512-01237.description: Abstract 1 Introduction Newton invented classical mechanics putting two time derivatives in his equation F=m\ddot{x} , which corresponds to a kinetic energy with 2 time derivatives, m\dot{x}^{2}/2 . Later Ostrogradski proofed a no-go theorem: non-degenerate classical systems with more than two time derivatives contain arbitrarily negative energies and develop fatal run-away instabilities [ 1 ] .

arxiv-2206-08125.title: Applications of topological cyclic homology to algebraic K-theory
arxiv-2206-08125.creator: Bjørn Ian Dundas
arxiv-2206-08125.description: Abstract A bstract. Algebraic K-theory has applications in a broad range of mathematical subjects, from number theory to functional analysis. It is also fiendishly hard to calculate. Presently there are two main inroads: motivic homotopy theory and cyclic homology. I’ve been asked to present an overview of the applications of topological cyclic homology to algebraic K-theory “from a historical perspective”.

arxiv-2304-04838.title: Multi-nucleon structure and dynamics via quantum computing
arxiv-2304-04838.creator: Weijie Du, James P. Vary
arxiv-2304-04838.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Weijie Du, James P. Vary. We propose a framework for computing the structure and dynamics for second-quantized many-nucleon Hamiltonians on quantum computers. We develop an oracle-based Hamiltonian input model that computes the many-nucleon states and nonzero Hamiltonian matrix elements of the many-nucleon system. With our Fock-state based input model, we show how to implement the sparse matrix simulation algorithms to calculate the dynamics of the second-quantized many-nucleon Hamiltonian.

arxiv-2408-06853.title: Better Gaussian Mechanism using Correlated Noise
arxiv-2408-06853.creator: Christian Janos Lebeda
arxiv-2408-06853.description: Abstract We present a simple variant of the Gaussian mechanism for answering differentially private queries when the sensitivity space has a certain common structure. Our motivating problem is the fundamental task of answering d d counting queries under the add/remove neighboring relation.

arxiv-2501-18429.title: SeqSee: A schema-based approach to spectral sequence visualization Thanks: The authors were partially supported by National Science Foundation Grant DMS-2202267.
arxiv-2501-18429.creator: Joey Beauvais-Feisthauer, Dan Isaksen
arxiv-2501-18429.description: Abstract . We present SeqSee , a software system that addresses spectral sequence visualization through a schema-based approach. By introducing a standardized JSON schema as an intermediate representation, SeqSee decouples the mathematical computations of spectral sequences from their visualizations. We demonstrate the system through a case study of the classical and ℂ \mathbb{C} -motivic Adams spectral sequences.

arxiv-2506-12510.title: Credit risk for large portfolios of green and brown loans: extending the ASRF model.
arxiv-2506-12510.creator: A. Ramponi, S. Scarlatti
arxiv-2506-12510.description: Abstract We propose a credit risk model for portfolios composed of green and brown loans, extending the ASRF framework via a two-factor copula structure. Systematic risk is modeled using potentially skewed distributions, allowing for asymmetric creditworthiness effects, while idiosyncratic risk remains Gaussian.

pmc-10670032.creator: Aurore Anton, Mathilde Plinet, Thomas Peyret, Thomas Cazaudarré, Stéphanie Pesant, Yannick Rouquet, Marie-Andrée Tricoteaux, Matthieu Bernier, Jérémy Bayette, Remi Fournier, Mélanie Marguerettaz, Pierre Rolland, Thibaud Bayol, Nadia Abbaoui, Antoine Berry, Xavier Iriart, Sophie Cassaing, Pamela Chau
pmc-10670032.description: Dermatophytosis is a superficial fungal infection with an ever-increasing number of patients. Therefore, routine clinical laboratories need rapid, high throughput, and accurate species-specific analytical methods for diagnosis and therapeutic management.

pmc-12357346.title: “The association of cardiometabolic diseases and related medications with cognitive performance: a cross-sectional observational study from Central Poland”
pmc-12357346.creator: Bartłomiej K Sołtysik, Anna Cieślak-Skubel, Agnieszka Gutowska, Elisio Costa, Tomasz Kostka
pmc-12357346.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionGlobal ageing, the rising prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases and dementia becomes increasingly important public health topic. This relation has evoked extensive research efforts aimed at finding the link between cardiovascular health and cognitive decline. Cardiometabolic medications, widely prescribed for their beneficial effects on vascular health, are being closely examined for their potential influence on cognitive health and their capacity to modify the risk of dementia.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, 1735 individuals from Central Poland were investigated on cardiometabolic diseases, treatments, and cognitive function.

pmc-12473419.title: Validation of Inertial Measurement Units for Measuring Lower-Extremity Kinematics During Squat–Pivot and Stoop–Twist Lifting Tasks
pmc-12473419.creator: Rutuja A Kulkarni, Rajit Banerjee, Vicki Z Wang, Marcel Oliart, Verity Rampulla, Prithvi Das, Alicia M Koontz, Stephen Klisch, Britta Berg-Johansen
pmc-12473419.description: Optokinetic motion capture (OMC) is the gold standard for measuring the kinematics associated with lifting posture. Unfortunately, limitations exist, including cost, portability, and marker occlusion. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the agreement between OMC and inertial measurement units (IMUs) for quantifying joint kinematics during squat–pivot and stoop–twist lifting tasks.
